# purr

Nix flake framework based on directory layout, namespaces, and modules

# purr

purr builds a Nix flake from the files in your project. It discovers modules, packages,
systems, homes, and the other outputs from the directory layout, so you do not have to
wire them together by hand.

purr depends on `nixpkgs-lib`. The standalone API is a single `mkFlake` call, and the
flake-parts module exposes the same discovery.

## Quick start

Start from a template:

```bash
# Standalone (mkFlake)
nix flake init -t github:nixcafe/purr

# With flake-parts
nix flake init -t github:nixcafe/purr#flake-parts
```

Or add purr to an existing flake:

```nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    purr.url = "https://flakehub.com/f/nixcafe/purr/0.1.*.tar.gz";
  };

  outputs = inputs:
    inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
      inherit inputs;
      src = ./.;
      namespace = "myproject";
    };
}
```

## What purr discovers

`src` is scanned for these directories:

```
.
├── flake.nix
├── modules/              → nixosModules, darwinModules, homeModules
├── packages/             → packages.<system>.* (also registered into pkgs.*)
├── legacyPackages/       → legacyPackages.<system>.*
├── shells/               → devShells.<system>.*
├── checks/               → checks.<system>.*
├── apps/                 → apps.<system>.*
├── overlays/             → overlays.*
├── templates/            → templates.*
├── formatters/           → formatter.<system>
├── hydraJobs/            → hydraJobs.* (when enabled)
├── lib/                  → lib.<namespace>.*
├── systems/              → nixosConfigurations, darwinConfigurations
└── homes/                → homeConfigurations
```

## Modules

Modules under `modules/` are exposed by their subdirectory path:

```
modules/
├── nixos/services/openssh/default.nix  → nixosModules.services.openssh
├── darwin/system/defaults/default.nix  → darwinModules.system.defaults
├── home/programs/git/default.nix       → homeModules.programs.git
└── shared/users/default.nix            → merged into nixos + darwin
```

The default `moduleTypes` maps `nixos/` and `shared/` to `nixosModules`, `darwin/` and
`shared/` to `darwinModules`, and `home/` to `homeModules`. See
[Module System](/modules) for the mappings and customisation.

## Namespaces

When `namespace` is set, purr passes it to every discovered module and exports the
project lib under `lib.<namespace>`:

```nix
{ config, lib, namespace, ... }:
let
  cfg = config.${namespace}.my-module;
in
{
  options.${namespace}.my-module.enable = lib.mkEnableOption "my module";
  config = lib.mkIf cfg.enable { /* ... */ };
}
```

## Shared lib

A `lib/` directory is available as `lib.<namespace>.*` in every module, package,
shell, and check:

```nix
# lib/default.nix
{ lib, inputs, namespace }:
{
  keys = import ./keys.nix { inherit lib inputs namespace; };
  utils = import ./utils.nix { inherit lib inputs namespace; };
}
```

Access the functions with `lib.<namespace>.keys`, `lib.<namespace>.utils`, and so on.

## Systems and homes

Systems and homes use the `<arch>-<format>/<name>` layout:

```
systems/
├── x86_64-linux/server/default.nix    → nixosConfigurations.server
└── aarch64-darwin/macbook/default.nix → darwinConfigurations.macbook

homes/
└── x86_64-linux/alice@server/default.nix  → homeConfigurations."alice@server"
```

A home named `<user>@<host>` is linked to the matching host when home-manager is
available. See [Systems & Homes](/systems-homes) and [Host Meta](/meta).

## hydraJobs

When enabled, `hydraJobs` mirrors buildable outputs and adds jobs from a `hydraJobs/`
directory. See [hydraJobs](/hydrajobs).

## Integration modes

* [flake-parts](/flake-parts): import `inputs.purr.flakeModules.default`.
* [mkFlake](/mkflake): call `inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake` without flake-parts.

## Project layout

See [Directory Structure](/directory-structure) for the full layout.

## API reference

The library exports 43 functions. See [API Reference](/api).

# flake-parts Integration

purr provides a [flake-parts](https://github.com/hercules-ci/flake-parts) module at
`inputs.purr.flakeModules.default`. It adds the `purr.*` options and builds the
discovered flake outputs.

## Setup

```nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    flake-parts.url = "github:hercules-ci/flake-parts";
    purr.url = "github:nixcafe/purr";
    my-extra-modules.url = "github:user/my-extra-modules";
  };

  outputs = inputs:
    inputs.flake-parts.lib.mkFlake { inherit inputs; } {
      imports = [ inputs.purr.flakeModules.default ];
      systems = [ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "aarch64-darwin" ];
      purr = {
        enable = true;
        src = ./.;
        namespace = "cattery";
        extraModules.nixos = [
          inputs.my-extra-modules.nixosModules.default
        ];
      };
    };
}
```

## Options

All options are under the `purr.*` namespace.

### Core options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `purr.enable` | bool | `false` | Enable purr |
| `purr.src` | path | required | Project root directory |
| `purr.namespace` | nullOr str | `null` | Module option namespace |
| `purr.libDir` | nullOr str | `null` | Path under `src` for the project lib; auto-detects `lib/` |
| `purr.flattenLib` | bool | `false` | Flatten lib subdirectories into the namespace root |
| `purr.modulesDir` | str | `"modules"` | Module directory name under `src` |
| `purr.moduleTypes` | attrs | See below | Subdirectory mapping per output |
| `purr.extraModules` | attrs | `{}` | `{ nixos = [...]; darwin = [...]; home = [...]; }` |
| `purr.extraArgs` | attrs | `{}` | Custom values added to the arguments of every auto-discovered module, system `specialArgs`, and home `extraSpecialArgs`. purr's own keys win on conflict |
| `purr.bundleModules` | bool | `false` | Include `extraModules` in the generated `default` module bundle |
| `purr.bundleExtraModules` | bool | `true` | Include extra modules in the bundle when `bundleModules` is on |

Default `moduleTypes`:

```nix
{
  nixos = ["nixos" "shared"];
  darwin = ["darwin" "shared"];
  home = ["home"];
}
```

### Directory options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `purr.checksDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `checks/` |
| `purr.shellsDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `shells/` then `devShells/` |
| `purr.overlaysDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `overlays/` |
| `purr.packagesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `packages/` |
| `purr.packagesByName` | bool | `false` | Also discover packages from `packages/by-name/<shard>/<name>/package.nix` |
| `purr.packagesToPkgs` | bool | `true` | Register discovered packages in `pkgs` as well. See [Packages](/mkflake#packages) |
| `purr.legacyPackagesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `legacyPackages/` |
| `purr.legacyPackagesByName` | bool | `false` | Also discover legacy packages from the `by-name/` layout |
| `purr.appsDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `apps/` |
| `purr.templatesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `templates/` |
| `purr.templatesRecursive` | bool | `false` | Scan `templates/` recursively |
| `purr.formatterDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `formatters/` then `formatter/`. The `default.nix` must return a derivation |
| `purr.systemsDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `systems/` then `hosts/` |
| `purr.homesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `homes/` |

### Other options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `purr.nixpkgsConfig` | attrs | `{}` | nixpkgs config such as `allowUnfree` |
| `purr.inputsFor` | nullOr fn | `null` | Filter or replace the flake inputs that purr uses internally. Accepts `{ inputs, ... } -> inputs'` or a plain attrset. Modules still receive the raw `inputs`. See [Per-host inputs](/mkflake#per-host-inputs-multi-nixpkgs) |
| `purr.autoInject` | bool | `true` | Inject `networking.hostName`, `home.username`, and `home.homeDirectory` with `lib.mkDefault` |
| `purr.outputsBuilder` | fn | `(_: {})` | Additional per-system outputs. Called with `{ pkgs, system, lib, inputs, namespace }` plus every `extraArgs` key. The result is deep-merged into the per-system outputs |
| `purr.hosts` | attrs | `{}` | Per-host config: `purr.hosts.<name>.meta = { images = [...]; deployable = true; roles.nixpkgs = "..."; ... }`, deep-merged over the host's `meta.nix`. See [Host Meta](/meta) |

### hydraJobs options

All under `purr.hydraJobs.*`. See the [hydraJobs](/hydrajobs) page for details.

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `purr.hydraJobs.enable` | bool | `false` | Enable the `hydraJobs` flake output |
| `purr.hydraJobs.as` | str | `"hydraJobs"` | Name of the flake output carrying the jobs |
| `purr.hydraJobs.dir` | nullOr str | `null` | Jobs directory; auto-detects `hydraJobs/` |
| `purr.hydraJobs.systems` | nullOr \[str] | `null` | Restrict CI jobs to these systems. Also restricts the top-level `images` output |
| `purr.hydraJobs.include` | nullOr \[str] | `null` | Outputs to mirror into hydraJobs; `null` auto-detects |
| `purr.hydraJobs.extra` | attrs | `{}` | Extra jobs merged last, highest priority |

## Custom module directories

Change which subdirectories are scanned for each module type:

```nix
purr.moduleTypes = {
  nixos = ["nixos" "shared" "container" "nixos-musl"];
};
```

## Extra modules from other flakes

Inject external modules alongside auto-discovered ones:

```nix
purr.extraModules = {
  nixos = [
    inputs.my-extra-modules.nixosModules.default
    inputs.disko.nixosModules.default
  ];
};
```

## Default module bundle

A `default` module that imports all discovered sub-modules is generated for
`nixosModules`, `darwinModules`, and `homeModules`. It is skipped when a discovered
module set or `extraModules` already defines `default`. Consumers can import the
bundle with:

```nix
{ imports = [ inputs.myflake.nixosModules.default ]; }
```

`bundleModules` (default `false`) controls whether `extraModules` are folded into this
bundle. Set it to `true` and leave `bundleExtraModules = true` to include them, or set
`bundleExtraModules = false` to bundle only the auto-discovered modules:

```nix
purr.bundleModules = true;        # include extraModules in the default bundle
purr.bundleExtraModules = false;  # only discovered modules in the bundle
```

## Formatter and legacy packages

Discovery works the same as in mkFlake. A `formatters/default.nix` that returns a
derivation becomes `formatter.<system>`, and `legacyPackages/<name>/default.nix`
becomes `legacyPackages.<system>.<name>`:

```nix
# formatters/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style

# legacyPackages/hello/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.hello
```

To also scan the `by-name/` layout for legacy packages:

```nix
purr.legacyPackagesByName = true;   # also scan legacyPackages/by-name/
```

Checks, shells, apps, overlays, and templates use the same directories and module
shapes as mkFlake. See [checks and shells](/mkflake#checks-and-shells),
[apps](/mkflake#apps), and
[overlays and templates](/mkflake#overlays-and-templates).

## Outputs builder

`purr.outputsBuilder` works like mkFlake's `outputsBuilder`. It receives
`{ pkgs, system, lib, inputs, namespace }` plus every `extraArgs` key, and its result
is deep-merged with the discovered per-system outputs:

```nix
purr.outputsBuilder = { pkgs, system, lib, namespace, ... }: {
  packages.fmt = pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style;
};
```

## Hydra CI

Generate a `hydraJobs` output that mirrors configuration outputs and adds custom jobs
from a `hydraJobs/` directory:

```nix
purr.hydraJobs = {
  enable = true;
  systems = ["x86_64-linux"];
  include = [ "nixosConfigurations" "homeConfigurations" ];
};
```

In flake-parts mode, hydraJobs mirrors the config outputs
(`nixosConfigurations`, `darwinConfigurations`, `homeConfigurations`), images,
directory jobs, and `extra`. The per-system outputs (`checks`, `packages`,
`devShells`, `legacyPackages`, `formatter`) are not auto-mirrored; add them through
`purr.hydraJobs.extra` if needed.

See the [hydraJobs](/hydrajobs) page for the full reference.

## Namespace lib output

When a `lib/` directory exists and `namespace` is set, purr exports the namespace lib
as a flake output in both mkFlake and flake-parts modes. When `namespace` is `null`,
the same lib is exported at `lib`:

```nix
# lib/default.nix
{ lib, inputs, namespace }:
{
  utils = import ./utils.nix { inherit lib inputs namespace; };
}
```

```bash
nix eval .#lib.myproject.utils
```

## Extra args

Pass custom values to every auto-discovered module:

```nix
purr.extraArgs = {
  deploymentTarget = "production";
};
```

Modules receive `extraArgs` values as function parameters:

```nix
# modules/nixos/server/default.nix
{ deploymentTarget, config, lib, ... }:
{
  services.nginx.virtualHosts."myapp" = lib.mkIf (deploymentTarget == "production") {
    # ...
  };
}
```

The keys are passed to packages, shells, checks, apps, templates, system
`specialArgs`, home `extraSpecialArgs`, and `outputsBuilder`. purr's own keys
(`inputs`, `pkgs`, `namespace`, `lib`, and similar) override `extraArgs` on conflict.

# mkFlake Usage

`mkFlake` builds a flake from a project directory without flake-parts. The call returns
the complete `outputs` attrset.

## Basic usage

```nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    purr.url = "github:nixcafe/purr";
  };

  outputs = inputs:
    inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
      inherit inputs;
      src = ./.;
      namespace = "myproject";
      outputsBuilder = { pkgs, ... }: {
        formatter = pkgs.nixfmt;
      };
    };
}
```

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `inputs` | attrs | required | Flake inputs. `nixpkgs` is required. `home-manager` (or `homeManager`) enables home-manager outputs, and `nix-darwin` (or `darwin`) enables darwin support |
| `inputsFor` | fn | identity | Filter or replace the flake inputs that purr uses internally. Accepts `{ inputs, ... } -> inputs'` or a plain attrset. Modules still receive the raw `inputs`. See [Per-host inputs](#per-host-inputs-multi-nixpkgs) |
| `src` | path | required | Project root directory |
| `namespace` | nullOr str | `null` | Module option namespace, also used as the lib key (`lib.<namespace>`) |
| `libDir` | nullOr str | `null` | Lib directory relative to `src`; auto-detects `lib/` |
| `flattenLib` | bool | `false` | Flatten lib subdirectories into the namespace root |
| `systems` | list | `["x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "aarch64-darwin"]` | Systems to generate per-system outputs for |
| `nixpkgsConfig` | attrs | `{}` | nixpkgs config such as `allowUnfree` |
| `outputsBuilder` | fn | `(_: {})` | Per-system extra outputs. Called with `{ pkgs, system, inputs, namespace, lib, ... }` plus every `extraArgs` key. The result is deep-merged with the discovered outputs |
| `modulesDir` | str | `"modules"` | Module directory name under `src` |
| `moduleTypes` | attrs | `{ nixos = [...]; darwin = [...]; home = [...]; }` | Subdirectory mapping per output |
| `extraModules` | attrs | `{}` | Raw module injection: `{ nixos = [...]; darwin = [...]; home = [...]; }` |
| `extraArgs` | attrs | `{}` | Custom values added to the arguments of every auto-discovered module, system `specialArgs`, and home `extraSpecialArgs`. purr's own keys win on conflict |
| `hosts` | attrs | `{}` | Per-host config: `hosts.<name>.meta = { images = [...]; deployable = true; roles.nixpkgs = "..."; ... }`, deep-merged over the host's `meta.nix`. See [Host Meta](/meta) |
| `bundleModules` | bool | `false` | Include `extraModules` in the generated `default` module bundle |
| `bundleExtraModules` | bool | `true` | Include extra modules in the bundle when `bundleModules` is on |
| `checksDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `checks/` |
| `shellsDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `shells/` then `devShells/` |
| `overlaysDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `overlays/` |
| `packagesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `packages/` |
| `packagesByName` | bool | `false` | Also discover packages from `packages/by-name/<shard>/<name>/package.nix` |
| `packagesToPkgs` | bool | `true` | Register discovered packages in `pkgs` as well. See [Packages](#packages) |
| `legacyPackagesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `legacyPackages/` |
| `legacyPackagesByName` | bool | `false` | Also discover legacy packages from the `by-name/` layout |
| `appsDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `apps/` |
| `templatesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `templates/` |
| `templatesRecursive` | bool | `false` | Scan `templates/` recursively |
| `formatterDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `formatters/` then `formatter/`. The `default.nix` must return a derivation |
| `systemsDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `systems/` then `hosts/` |
| `homesDir` | nullOr str | `null` | auto-detects `homes/` |
| `autoInject` | bool | `true` | Inject `networking.hostName`, `home.username`, and `home.homeDirectory` with `lib.mkDefault` |
| `hydraJobs` | attrs | `{}` | Hydra CI options: `{ enable, as, dir, systems, include, extra }`. See below |

## Hydra CI

`hydraJobs` mirrors buildable outputs and adds jobs from a `hydraJobs/` directory:

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  hydraJobs = {
    enable = true;
    systems = ["x86_64-linux"];
    include = [ "checks" "packages" "nixosConfigurations" ];
  };
}
```

See the [hydraJobs](/hydrajobs) page for the full reference.

## Customizing systems

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  systems = [ "x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" ];
}
```

## Custom module directories

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  moduleTypes = {
    nixos = ["nixos" "shared" "container"];
  };
}
```

## Systems and homes

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  systemsDir = "systems";   # or "hosts", or null to auto-detect
  homesDir = "homes";
}
```

## Per-host inputs (multi-nixpkgs)

`inputsFor` selects which inputs purr builds from. A host then points at one of those
inputs with `meta.roles.<role>`. Modules always keep the original `inputs` argument.
The replacement only affects how purr builds pkgs, system configs, home configs, and
the merged lib. See [Host Meta: roles](/meta#roles-per-host-inputs) for the role
reference.

```nix
# flake.nix
{
  inputs = {
    nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-25.05";
    nixpkgs-unstable.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable";
    purr.url = "github:nixcafe/purr";
  };

  outputs = inputs:
    inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
      inherit inputs;
      src = ./.;
      inputsFor = { inputs, ... }: {
        inherit (inputs) nixpkgs;
        inherit (inputs) nixpkgs-unstable;
      };
      hosts.server.meta.roles.nixpkgs = "nixpkgs-unstable";
    };
}
```

The same role can be set in `meta.nix`:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{ roles.nixpkgs = "nixpkgs-unstable"; }
```

Supported role keys are `nixpkgs`, `home-manager`, and `nix-darwin`. Homes inherit
their linked system's nixpkgs; unmatched homes use the effective-input default.

## Formatter

A per-system formatter is discovered from `formatters/` or `formatter/`. The
`default.nix` receives `{ pkgs, lib, system, namespace, inputs, ... }` and must return
a derivation:

```nix
# formatters/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style
```

This produces `formatter.<system>`, which `nix fmt` uses. `outputsBuilder` can override
it:

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  outputsBuilder = { pkgs, ... }: {
    formatter = pkgs.alejandra;
  };
}
```

## Packages

Modules under `packages/` are exposed as `packages.<system>.<name>`. When
`packagesToPkgs = true` (the default), they are also registered in `pkgs`, so any
per-system module or host config can reference them as `pkgs.<name>`:

```nix
# packages/hello/default.nix
{ lib, ... }: { /* ... */ }
```

```nix
# checks/lint/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.hello   # the discovered package
```

Each discovered package is wrapped like a `callPackage` package, so
`.override` and `.overrideAttrs` work, and packages can depend on each other:

```nix
# packages/wrapper/default.nix
# `hello` resolves from `pkgs`
{ hello, ... }: hello.override { /* ... */ }
```

Registration is a nixpkgs overlay built on the package-set fixpoint. One-way
dependencies resolve lazily. Mutually recursive packages recurse, as in any nixpkgs
overlay.

Set `packagesToPkgs = false` to keep packages out of `pkgs`. They remain available as
`packages.<system>.<name>`:

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  packagesToPkgs = false;
}
```

## Legacy packages

`legacyPackages.<system>.*` is discovered from `legacyPackages/`. These packages are
not added to `pkgs`:

```nix
# legacyPackages/hello/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.hello
```

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  legacyPackagesByName = true;   # also scan legacyPackages/by-name/<shard>/<name>/package.nix
}
```

Build one with `nix build .#legacyPackages.<system>.hello`.

## Checks and shells

`checks/<name>/default.nix` becomes `checks.<system>.<name>`, and
`shells/<name>/default.nix` becomes `devShells.<system>.<name>`:

```nix
# checks/lint/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.runCommand "lint" { } "true"

# shells/dev/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.mkShell { packages = [ pkgs.git ]; }
```

## Apps

`apps/<name>/default.nix` becomes `apps.<system>.<name>` and must return a flake app:

```nix
# apps/hello/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: {
  type = "app";
  program = "${pkgs.hello}/bin/hello";
}
```

## Overlays and templates

`overlays/<name>/default.nix` becomes `overlays.<name>`, and
`templates/<name>/default.nix` becomes `templates.<name>`:

```nix
# overlays/custom/default.nix
_final: prev: {
  hello = prev.hello.overrideAttrs (_: { doCheck = false; });
}

# templates/rust/default.nix
{
  path = ./.;
  description = "A Rust project";
}
```

## Extra args

Pass custom values to every auto-discovered module:

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  extraArgs = {
    deploymentTarget = "production";
  };
}
```

Modules receive `extraArgs` values as function parameters:

```nix
# packages/myapp/default.nix
{ deploymentTarget, pkgs, ... }:
pkgs.writeText "myapp" "target: ${deploymentTarget}"
```

The keys are passed to packages, shells, checks, apps, templates, system
`specialArgs`, home `extraSpecialArgs`, and `outputsBuilder`. purr's own keys
(`inputs`, `pkgs`, `namespace`, `lib`, and similar) override `extraArgs` on conflict.

# Module System

purr discovers modules from the directory layout and exports them as flake module
outputs. Modules are plain Nix modules; purr supplies the namespace and the project
lib.

## Module discovery

Place modules under `modules/`. The path below the module type directory becomes the
attribute path:

```
modules/
├── nixos/services/openssh/default.nix  → nixosModules.services.openssh
├── darwin/system/defaults/default.nix  → darwinModules.system.defaults
├── home/programs/git/default.nix       → homeModules.programs.git
└── shared/users/default.nix            → nixos + darwin (shared)
```

### Module types

The default mapping decides which subdirectories go to which flake outputs:

| Output | Directories |
|--------|-------------|
| `nixosModules` | `nixos/`, `shared/` |
| `darwinModules` | `darwin/`, `shared/` |
| `homeModules` | `home/` |

Change it with `moduleTypes`:

```nix
moduleTypes = {
  nixos = ["nixos" "shared" "container" "nixos-musl"];
};
```

A directory is included only if it exists. Modules from all listed directories are
merged into the same output tree.

## Namespace

When `namespace` is set, each module receives it as a parameter. Options stay under
`config.<namespace>.*`:

```nix
{ config, lib, namespace, ... }@args:
let
  cfg = config.${namespace}.my-module;
in
{
  options.${namespace}.my-module.enable = lib.mkEnableOption "my module";
  config = lib.mkIf cfg.enable { ... };
}
```

The namespace wrapper also injects the defining flake's `inputs` and the merged lib,
so modules can use `lib.<namespace>.*` without an extra import.

## Module arguments

Auto-discovered modules receive different arguments depending on their directory:

| Directory | Arguments |
|-----------|-----------|
| `lib/` | `{ lib, inputs, namespace }` |
| `modules/` | `{ config, options, lib, pkgs, namespace, ... }` |
| `packages/` | `{ inputs, system, namespace, lib, pkgs, ... }` |
| `legacyPackages/` | `{ inputs, system, namespace, lib, pkgs, ... }` |
| `shells/` | `{ inputs, system, namespace, lib, pkgs, ... }` |
| `checks/` | `{ inputs, system, namespace, lib, pkgs, ... }` |
| `apps/` | `{ inputs, system, namespace, lib, pkgs, ... }` |
| `formatters/` or `formatter/` | `{ inputs, system, namespace, lib, pkgs, ... }` |
| `overlays/` | `final: prev:` |
| `templates/` | `{ inputs, namespace, lib, ... }` |
| `systems/` | `{ config, options, lib, pkgs, purr, host, namespace, system, inputs, ... }` |
| `homes/` | `{ config, options, lib, pkgs, purr, user, host, namespace, system, inputs, ... }` |

`lib` in `packages/`, `legacyPackages/`, `shells/`, `checks/`, `apps/`, and
`formatters/` is the merged lib, including the project lib under
`lib.<namespace>.*`. `systems/` and `homes/` receive `purr` through `specialArgs`
and `extraSpecialArgs`. See [Systems & Homes](/systems-homes#purr-metadata) for the
shape of `purr`.

Discovered packages are registered in `pkgs` by default (`packagesToPkgs = true`) and
the whole `pkgs` set is passed to per-system modules. A package can therefore depend
on a sibling package by name: `{ hello, ... }: hello.override { ... }`. This applies
to per-system modules, not to NixOS or home modules, which use `pkgs.<name>`. See
[Packages](/mkflake#packages).

## Custom lib

Create a `lib/` directory under `src` to share functions across modules:

```nix
# lib/default.nix
{ lib, inputs, namespace }:
{
  keys = import ./keys.nix { inherit lib inputs namespace; };
  utils = import ./utils.nix { inherit lib inputs namespace; };
}
```

The functions are available as `lib.<namespace>.*` in modules, packages, shells,
checks, apps, templates, formatters, and legacy packages:

```nix
# packages/known-hosts/default.nix
{ pkgs, lib, namespace, ... }:
let
  inherit (lib.${namespace}) keys;
in
pkgs.writeText "known-hosts" (keys.generate { ... })
```

Subdirectories nest by default (`lib.<namespace>.keys.foo`). Set `flattenLib = true`
to merge all submodules directly under the namespace (`lib.<namespace>.foo`). When
`namespace` is `null`, the lib is merged at the top level of `lib`.

A root `lib/default.nix` and subdirectory modules can coexist. The root module is
imported separately by `buildImportedPurrLib`; subdirectory modules are collected by
`findModulesLib`.

## Default module bundle

A `default` module that imports all discovered sub-modules is generated for
`nixosModules`, `darwinModules`, and `homeModules`. It is skipped when a discovered
module set or `extraModules` already defines `default`:

```nix
{ imports = [ inputs.myflake.nixosModules.default ]; }
```

`bundleModules` (default `false`) controls whether `extraModules` are folded into the
bundle. Set `bundleModules = true` to include them, and `bundleExtraModules = false`
to bundle only the auto-discovered modules.

## Extra modules

Inject modules from other flakes:

```nix
extraModules = {
  nixos = [
    inputs.my-extra-modules.nixosModules.default
    inputs.disko.nixosModules.default
  ];
};
```

# Directory Structure

purr resolves each directory under the project `src` path. Most directories are
optional; a directory is used when it exists.

```
src/
├── lib/                              # Project library (auto-detect: "lib")
│   ├── default.nix                   #   { lib, inputs, namespace }: returns an attrset
│   ├── keys/
│   │   └── default.nix               #   nested → lib.<namespace>.keys
│   └── utils/
│       └── default.nix               #   nested → lib.<namespace>.utils
│                                     #   flattenLib = true → lib.<namespace>
│
├── modules/                          # NixOS/darwin/home modules
│   ├── nixos/                        #   → nixosModules
│   ├── darwin/                       #   → darwinModules
│   ├── home/                         #   → homeModules
│   └── shared/                       #   → merged into nixos + darwin
│
├── packages/                         # Per-system packages (auto-detect: "packages")
│   │                                 #   also registered into pkgs.<name> (packagesToPkgs)
│   ├── known-hosts/
│   │   └── default.nix               #   → packages.<system>.known-hosts, pkgs.known-hosts
│   ├── match-blocks/
│   │   └── default.nix               #   → packages.<system>.match-blocks, pkgs.match-blocks
│   └── by-name/                      #   Optional by-name layout (packagesByName = true)
│       └── co/
│           └── cowsay/
│               └── package.nix       #   → packages.<system>.cowsay, pkgs.cowsay
│
├── legacyPackages/                   # Per-system legacy packages (auto-detect: "legacyPackages")
│   ├── hello/
│   │   └── default.nix               #   → legacyPackages.<system>.hello
│   └── by-name/                      #   Optional by-name layout (legacyPackagesByName = true)
│       └── he/
│           └── hello/
│               └── package.nix       #   → legacyPackages.<system>.hello
│
├── shells/                           # Dev shells (auto-detect: "shells", "devShells")
│   └── default/
│       └── default.nix               #   → devShells.<system>.default
│
├── checks/                           # Per-system checks (auto-detect: "checks")
│   └── pre-commit/
│       └── default.nix               #   → checks.<system>.pre-commit
│
├── overlays/                         # Overlays (auto-detect: "overlays")
│   └── custom/
│       └── default.nix               #   → overlays.custom
│
├── templates/                        # Flake templates (auto-detect: "templates")
│   └── rust/                         #   non-recursive by default
│       └── default.nix               #   → templates.rust
│
├── apps/                             # Per-system apps (auto-detect: "apps")
│   └── serve/
│       └── default.nix               #   → apps.<system>.serve
│
├── formatters/                       # Formatter (auto-detect: "formatters", "formatter")
│   └── default.nix                   #   returns a derivation → formatter.<system>
│                                     #   e.g. { pkgs, ... }: pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style
│
├── hydraJobs/                        # Custom CI jobs (used when hydraJobs.enable = true)
│   └── build/
│       └── hello/
│           └── default.nix           #   → hydraJobs.build.<system>.hello
│
├── systems/                          # auto-detect: "systems", "hosts"
│   └── x86_64-linux/
│       ├── server/default.nix        # → nixosConfigurations.server
│       └── server/meta.nix           #   optional host meta (see Host Meta)
│                                     #   e.g. { images = ["iso"]; }
│
└── homes/                            # auto-detect: "homes"
    └── x86_64-linux/
        └── alice@server/default.nix  # → homeConfigurations."alice@server"
```

Packages under `packages/` are also registered in `pkgs` as `pkgs.<name>`, so any
per-system module can use them. Disable this with `packagesToPkgs = false`. See
[Packages](/mkflake#packages).

Custom CI jobs live in `hydraJobs/` and are used when `hydraJobs.enable = true`. See
the [hydraJobs](/hydrajobs) page.

## Directory discovery

Each optional directory is resolved from the option value or from the candidate list
when the option is `null`. `modulesDir` is a name with the default `"modules"`, not an
auto-detected path.

| Output | Option | Auto-detect candidates |
|--------|--------|------------------------|
| Library | `libDir` | `lib/` |
| Modules | `modulesDir` | `"modules"` (default) |
| Checks | `checksDir` | `checks/` |
| Shells | `shellsDir` | `shells/` → `devShells/` |
| Overlays | `overlaysDir` | `overlays/` |
| Packages | `packagesDir` | `packages/` |
| Legacy packages | `legacyPackagesDir` | `legacyPackages/` |
| Apps | `appsDir` | `apps/` |
| Templates | `templatesDir` | `templates/` |
| Formatter | `formatterDir` | `formatters/` → `formatter/` |
| Systems | `systemsDir` | `systems/` → `hosts/` |
| Homes | `homesDir` | `homes/` |
| Hydra jobs | `hydraJobs.dir` | `hydraJobs/` |

Override any directory with an explicit name:

```nix
# mkFlake
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  shellsDir = "myshells";
  systemsDir = "hosts";
}

# flake-parts
purr = {
  enable = true;
  src = ./.;
  shellsDir = "myshells";
  systemsDir = "hosts";
};
```

# Systems & Homes

purr discovers NixOS and darwin systems from `<arch>-<format>/<name>` and
home-manager homes from `<arch>-<format>/<user>@<host>`. Only the `linux` and `darwin`
formats are supported.

## Directory layout

```
src/
├── systems/                          # auto-detect: "systems", "hosts"
│   ├── x86_64-linux/
│   │   ├── server/default.nix        # → nixosConfigurations.server
│   │   └── laptop/default.nix        # → nixosConfigurations.laptop
│   └── aarch64-darwin/
│       └── macbook/default.nix       # → darwinConfigurations.macbook
│
├── homes/                            # auto-detect: "homes"
│   ├── x86_64-linux/
│   │   ├── alice@server/default.nix  # → homeConfigurations."alice@server"
│   │   └── bob@server/default.nix    # → homeConfigurations."bob@server"
│   └── aarch64-darwin/
│       └── alice@macbook/default.nix # → homeConfigurations."alice@macbook"
```

## Output mapping

| Format in directory name | Flake output key | Builder |
|---|---|---|
| `linux` | `nixosConfigurations.<name>` | `nixosSystem` |
| `darwin` | `darwinConfigurations.<name>` | `darwinSystem` |

## Home auto-linking

Homes named `<user>@<host>` are linked to the matching system. When `home-manager`
(or `homeManager`) is available as an input, building `nixosConfigurations.server`
includes every home with the `@server` suffix:

```nix
# homes/x86_64-linux/alice@server/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: {
  home.packages = [ pkgs.neovim ];
  programs.git.enable = true;
}
```

The home is added through `home-manager.users.alice` in the host's NixOS
configuration. For every linked home, purr also:

* sets `home-manager.useGlobalPkgs` and `home-manager.useUserPackages` to
  `mkDefault true`
* creates `users.users.<name>` (`isNormalUser = mkDefault true`) for non-root users on
  Linux hosts
* passes the username as `_module.args.user` and injects `home.username` and
  `home.homeDirectory` as defaults

## Building images

purr does not use special format directories such as `x86_64-iso`. nixpkgs 25.05 and
later imports `image/images.nix` by default, so every NixOS configuration exposes
`system.build.images`. Put the system under `systems/<arch>-linux/` and build an image
from it:

```bash
# ISO image
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.server.config.system.build.images.iso

# QEMU qcow2 image (EFI)
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.server.config.system.build.images.qemu-efi

# Raw disk image
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.server.config.system.build.images.raw

# DigitalOcean image
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.server.config.system.build.images.digital-ocean

# Amazon EC2 AMI
nix build .#nixosConfigurations.server.config.system.build.images.amazon
```

### Short `images.<host>.<format>` output

Declare the formats for a Linux host in its [host meta](/meta), either in `meta.nix`
or in `hosts.<name>.meta`. purr then exposes a top-level
`images.<host>.<format>` output:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{
  images = [ "iso" "qemu" ];
}
```

```bash
nix build .#images.server.iso
nix build .#images.server.qemu
```

This output exists whether or not hydraJobs is enabled. When `hydraJobs.systems` is
set, it also filters the `images` output. When hydraJobs is enabled, the same
declarations are mirrored as `hydraJobs.images.<host>.<format>`.

### Image-only hosts

On Linux, a host that declares `images` in its meta is an image-only recipe by default.
It is excluded from `nixosConfigurations` and `darwinConfigurations`, and from the
hydraJobs config groups. Its `system.build.toplevel` is never evaluated, so it cannot
be deployed with `nixos-rebuild`. Use this for hosts such as installer ISOs that have
no root file system:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/installer/meta.nix
{
  images = [ "iso" ];
}
```

`installer` does not appear in `nixosConfigurations`, but
`nix build .#images.installer.iso` works. Meta is read from `meta.nix` before nixpkgs
or home-manager is evaluated, and the image derivations stay lazy.

To keep a host deployable and build images from it, set `deployable = true`:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{
  images = [ "iso" "qemu" ];
  deployable = true;
}
```

`deployable` is a host meta key, not a system option. A host is deployable by default
when `images` is empty, or when the host is darwin. On Linux, declaring `images`
without `deployable = true` makes the host image-only.

### Available image formats

These formats come from nixpkgs `image/images.nix`:

| Format key | Image type | Format key | Image type |
|---|---|---|---|
| `iso` | Bootable ISO 9660 | `proxmox` | Proxmox VE image |
| `iso-installer` | Installer ISO | `proxmox-lxc` | Proxmox LXC container |
| `qemu-efi` | QEMU qcow2 (EFI) | `lxc` | LXC container |
| `qemu` | QEMU qcow2 (BIOS) | `lxc-metadata` | LXC metadata tarball |
| `raw-efi` | Raw disk (EFI) | `oci` | OCI container image |
| `raw` | Raw disk (BIOS) | `vagrant-virtualbox` | Vagrant VirtualBox |
| `amazon` | AWS EC2 AMI | `virtualbox` | VirtualBox OVA |
| `azure` | Azure VM image | `vmware` | VMware VMDK |
| `google-compute` | GCP image | `kubevirt` | KubeVirt container disk |
| `digital-ocean` | DigitalOcean image | `cloudstack` | Apache CloudStack |
| `hyperv` | Hyper-V VHDX | `openstack` | OpenStack image |
| `linode` | Linode image | `openstack-zfs` | OpenStack image with ZFS |
| `kexec` | Netboot kexec image | `sd-card` | Raspberry Pi / SD card |

### Different configs for different images

Put multiple systems under `systems/x86_64-linux/` with different names. A minimal
installer config is a good candidate for an image-only host:

```
systems/x86_64-linux/
  ├── production/default.nix   # full server
  └── installer/default.nix    # minimal ISO config
```

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/installer/meta.nix
{
  images = [ "iso" ];
}
```

Then build:

```bash
nix build .#images.installer.iso
```

## Namespace bridge (system to home config)

On a host with linked homes, purr defines the option `purr.users`. Setting
`purr.users.<name>.homeConfig` from any NixOS module forwards that config to
`home-manager.users.<name>`. The option exists whether or not a `namespace` is set:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/default.nix
{ config, pkgs, lib, purr, ... }:
{
  networking.hostName = purr.meta.name;

  purr.users.alice.homeConfig = {
    home.packages = [ pkgs.cowsay ];
    programs.git.userName = "Alice";
  };
}
```

Keys inside `homeConfig` map directly to home-manager option paths
(`home.packages`, `programs.*`, `services.*`, and so on). The bridge config is
forwarded as a normal-priority home-manager module. If both the bridge and the home
module set the same non-mergeable option at normal priority, the module system reports
a conflict. Use `lib.mkDefault` on one side when the home module should be able to
override a bridge value.

The bridge is added before the home module in the import list. Import order does not
change option priority.

## `purr` metadata

Each system and home module receives a `purr` attrset with metadata about the current
configuration. It is passed through `specialArgs` for systems and `extraSpecialArgs`
for homes.

### System modules (`specialArgs.purr`)

| Field | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `meta` | see [Host Meta](/meta) | Merged host metadata: `name`, `host`, `arch`, `archFormat`, `format`, `isDarwin`, `isLinux`, `system`, `homes`, `images`, `deployable`, `roles`, plus custom keys |
| `systemMetas` | `{ server = {...}; workstation = {...}; }` | Registry of every discovered host's merged meta, keyed by host name, including the current host |

### Home modules (`extraSpecialArgs.purr`)

| Field | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `meta` | `{ user = "alice"; host = "server"; ... }` | Standalone homes: home metadata (`user`, `host`, `arch`, `archFormat`, `format`, `isDarwin`, `isLinux`, `system`). Bridged homes: the host's merged meta, as described in [Host Meta](/meta) |
| `systemMeta` | see [Host Meta](/meta) | Merged meta of the system named by the home's host, or `null` when no matching system exists. In a bridged home this is the same host meta passed as `meta` |
| `systemMetas` | `{ server = {...}; ... }` | The same host registry that systems receive |
| `lib` | `{ hm = {...}; ... }` | The merged namespace lib with home-manager's `lib.hm` extension, also available as `lib` for standalone homes |

Bridged homes receive the host's merged meta as `purr.meta`, so `purr.meta.user` is
not set there. Use the `user` module argument in home modules that run both
standalone and bridged.

`purr.lib` is the merged namespace lib with `lib.hm` re-added. It is available in
both standalone and bridged homes, so `purr.lib.<namespace>.xxx` works from any home
module. Bridged homes keep home-manager's own evaluation lib and do not receive a
`lib` override. Standalone homes also receive their evaluation lib as `lib`;
`purr.lib` follows the home's resolved nixpkgs role.

### Usage

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/default.nix
{ config, pkgs, lib, purr, ... }:
{
  networking.hostName = purr.meta.name;              # "server"
  nixpkgs.hostPlatform = purr.meta.archFormat;       # "x86_64-linux"
  services.foo.enable = purr.meta.tier == "prod";    # custom meta key
  services.bar.enable = purr.systemMetas.workstation.tier == "dev";
}
```

```nix
# homes/x86_64-linux/alice@server/default.nix
{ pkgs, lib, purr, ... }:
{
  home.packages = [ pkgs.neovim ];
  # systemMeta is the meta of "server", or null when not linked to a system
  programs.git.enable = purr.systemMeta != null;
}
```

## Auto-injection

By default (`autoInject = true`), purr injects basic configuration with
`lib.mkDefault`, so user modules can override it:

| Context | Injected config |
|---|---|
| System config | `networking.hostName = <purr.meta.name>` |
| Home config (linux) | `home.username`, `home.homeDirectory = "/home/<user>"` |
| Home config (darwin) | `home.username`, `home.homeDirectory = "/Users/<user>"` |

Disable the defaults with `autoInject = false`.

## Usage in mkFlake

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  systemsDir = "systems";   # or "hosts", or null to auto-detect
  homesDir = "homes";
}
```

## Usage in flake-parts

```nix
purr = {
  enable = true;
  src = ./.;
  systemsDir = "systems";
  homesDir = "homes";
};
```

# Host Meta

Every system host can carry metadata that purr reads during flake evaluation and
passes to the host's modules as `purr.meta`. The same data decides which images to
build and whether the host is exposed as a configuration.

## Why host meta

Host declarations used to live in the host's `default.nix`. purr had to import the
module with placeholder arguments to read them, which could fail when the module
touched `config` or `pkgs` at the top level. Host meta is a separate file or config
value that purr reads directly. The host module is not imported to decide how the
host is exposed.

## Sources and merge order

Host meta is merged from up to three sources. Later sources win:

1. Auto-generated: `name`, `host`, `arch`, `archFormat`, `format`, `isDarwin`,
   `isLinux`, `system`, and `homes`. These come from the host's directory path and
   matched homes.
2. `meta.nix`: a file next to the host's `default.nix`.
3. `hosts.<name>.meta`: flake-level config (`hosts` in `mkFlake`, `purr.hosts` in
   flake-parts).

The two user sources are deep-merged with `lib.recursiveUpdate`, so a flake-level
config can override one nested key without replacing the whole attrset.

```
auto meta -> meta.nix -> hosts.<name>.meta
 (lowest)                  (highest)
```

## `meta.nix`

Place `meta.nix` next to the host's
`systems/<arch>-<format>/<name>/default.nix`:

```
src/
└── systems/
    └── x86_64-linux/
        └── server/
            ├── default.nix
            └── meta.nix          # optional host metadata
```

### Plain attrset

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{
  images = [ "iso" "qemu" ];
  tier = "prod";
}
```

### Function

`meta.nix` may also be a function. purr calls it with the auto-generated meta plus
fixed values. The arguments are bound lazily, so conditions such as
`if inputs ? nix-darwin then ...` do not force nixpkgs or the module system:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{ inputs, lib, arch, ... }:
assert lib != null;
if arch == "x86_64" && inputs ? home-manager then
  {
    images = [ "iso" "qemu" ];
    tier = "prod";
  }
else
  { images = [ ]; tier = "dev"; }
```

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| `inputs` | The flake inputs |
| `lib` | The merged purr lib (nixpkgs lib plus the namespace lib) |
| `namespace` | The configured namespace, or `null` |
| `extraArgs` | The configured `extraArgs` |
| `host` / `name` | Host name |
| `system` | Full triple, for example `"x86_64-linux"` |
| `arch` | Architecture, for example `"x86_64"` |
| `archFormat` | Directory name, for example `"x86_64-linux"` |
| `format` | `"linux"` or `"darwin"` |
| `isDarwin` / `isLinux` | Platform booleans |
| `homes` | Matched homes, for example `[{ user = "alice"; host = "server"; }]` |
| `...` | Extra arguments are accepted but not forced |

`pkgs`, `config`, and `options` are not provided. Meta evaluation does not evaluate a
NixOS or home-manager configuration.

## `hosts.<name>.meta`

### mkFlake

```nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  hosts.server.meta = {
    tier = "prod";      # deep-merges over meta.nix
  };
}
```

### flake-parts

```nix
purr.hosts.server.meta = {
  tier = "prod";
};
```

Referencing a host that has no matching
`systems/<arch>-<format>/<name>/default.nix` is an error.

## Reserved keys

The auto-generated keys cannot be overridden. Setting one in `meta.nix` or
`hosts.<name>.meta` emits a warning during flake evaluation and drops the user value.

| Reserved key | Auto-generated value |
|---|---|
| `name` | Host name |
| `host` | Host name (alias of `name`) |
| `arch` | Architecture |
| `archFormat` | Arch-format directory name |
| `format` | `"linux"` or `"darwin"` |
| `isDarwin` / `isLinux` | Platform booleans |
| `system` | Full triple |
| `homes` | Matched homes |

## Behaviour keys

These keys are consumed by purr:

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `images` | list of strings | Image formats to build for a Linux host. Exposed as `images.<host>.<format>`, and as `hydraJobs.images.<host>.<format>` when hydraJobs is enabled. Each format maps to `config.system.build.images.<format>` |
| `deployable` | bool | Whether the host is exposed in `nixosConfigurations` or `darwinConfigurations`. Defaults to `true` when `images` is empty or the host is darwin |
| `roles` | attrs | Maps a role name to a key of the effective inputs, for example `roles.nixpkgs = "nixpkgs-stable"`. See [roles](#roles-per-host-inputs) |

A Linux host with `images` and no explicit `deployable` is image-only. It is excluded
from the configuration outputs and the hydraJobs config groups, so its
`system.build.toplevel` is not evaluated. See
[Image-only hosts](/systems-homes#image-only-hosts).

### roles (per-host inputs)

Different hosts can build from different inputs, for example a second nixpkgs or a
different home-manager. Two pieces work together:

1. `inputsFor` filters or replaces the raw flake inputs into the effective inputs
   that purr builds from internally. See
   [mkFlake](/mkflake#per-host-inputs-multi-nixpkgs) or
   [flake-parts](/flake-parts). Default is the identity.
2. `meta.roles.<role>` points a host at an effective-input key. The role names
   (`nixpkgs`, `home-manager`, `nix-darwin`) live under `roles` so they do not collide
   with custom meta keys. If a role is absent, purr falls back to the conventional
   input key (`nixpkgs`, `home-manager` or `homeManager`, `nix-darwin` or `darwin`).

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{
  roles.nixpkgs = "nixpkgs-stable";
  roles."home-manager" = "home-manager-stable";
  tier = "prod";
}
```

Role replacement is internal. It changes which input purr uses to build pkgs, system
configs, home configs, and the merged lib base. The `inputs` argument that modules
receive is never modified. Homes inherit their linked system's nixpkgs; unmatched
homes use the effective-input default. Referencing an input that is missing from the
effective inputs throws an error.

## `purr.meta`

For system modules, the merged meta is passed through `specialArgs.purr.meta`. The
home-manager bridge receives the same host meta through `extraSpecialArgs`. It always
contains the 9 auto-generated keys plus the normalized `images` and derived
`deployable`, plus any custom keys:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/default.nix
{ purr, ... }:
{
  networking.hostName = purr.meta.name;     # "server"
  services.foo.enable = purr.meta.tier == "prod";
  system.stateVersion = "24.11";
}
```

```nix
purr.meta =
  {
    name = "server";
    host = "server";
    arch = "x86_64";
    archFormat = "x86_64-linux";
    format = "linux";
    isDarwin = false;
    isLinux = true;
    system = "x86_64-linux";
    homes = [ { user = "alice"; host = "server"; } ];
    images = [ "iso" "qemu" ];
    deployable = true;
    tier = "prod";      # custom key
  }
```

### `purr.systemMetas`

Every discovered host's merged meta is registered in `purr.systemMetas`, a pure
metadata registry keyed by host name. The registry includes the current host and is
available to both system and home modules. Reading another host's facts does not
evaluate that host's config:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/default.nix
{ purr, ... }:
{
  services.bar.enable = purr.systemMetas.workstation.tier == "dev";
}
```

Home modules also get `purr.systemMeta`, the merged meta of the system named by the
home's host, or `null` when no matching system exists.

### Custom keys

Any key other than the reserved and behaviour keys is passed through and exposed as
`purr.meta.<key>`. This is a free-form slot for labels, groups, feature flags, or
other data that both purr and your modules need to read.

## Validation

* `images` must be a list, otherwise evaluation throws.
* `meta.nix` must evaluate to an attrset, otherwise evaluation throws.
* `hosts.<name>.meta` referencing a nonexistent host throws.
* Reserved keys are dropped with a warning, not an error.

## Homes

Standalone home modules receive `purr.meta` with home-specific fields (`user`,
`host`, `arch`, `archFormat`, `format`, `isDarwin`, `isLinux`, `system`). They do not
receive the full host meta, so `images` and `deployable` are absent. Bridged homes
receive the host's merged meta as both `purr.meta` and `purr.systemMeta`; use the
`user` module argument for the username there. In both forms `purr.systemMetas` is the
host registry, and `purr.systemMeta` is the linked system's merged meta (or `null` for
an unlinked standalone home). See
[Systems & Homes: purr metadata](/systems-homes#purr-metadata).

# hydraJobs

purr can generate a `hydraJobs` flake output for [Hydra CI](https://nixos.org/hydra/).
Hydra evaluates `outputs.hydraJobs` (falling back to `checks`) and builds every
derivation leaf. When enabled, purr mirrors the buildable outputs and can add custom
jobs from a `hydraJobs/` directory.

## Enabling

hydraJobs is off by default. Enable it with `hydraJobs.enable`:

```nix
# mkFlake
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  hydraJobs.enable = true;
}

# flake-parts
purr = {
  enable = true;
  src = ./.;
  hydraJobs.enable = true;
};
```

## Options

### mkFlake

```nix
hydraJobs = {
  enable = true;                  # bool, default false: output hydraJobs
  as = "builds";                  # str, default "hydraJobs": output name
  dir = "hydraJobs";              # nullOr str, default null: auto-detects "hydraJobs"
  systems = ["x86_64-linux"];     # nullOr [str], default null: filter CI systems
  include = null;                 # nullOr [str], default null: auto-detect outputs
  extra = { };                    # attrs, default {}: extra jobs, highest priority
};
```

### flake-parts

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `purr.hydraJobs.enable` | bool | `false` | Enable the hydraJobs flake output |
| `purr.hydraJobs.as` | str | `"hydraJobs"` | Name of the flake output carrying the jobs |
| `purr.hydraJobs.dir` | nullOr str | `null` | Directory for custom jobs; auto-detects `hydraJobs/` |
| `purr.hydraJobs.systems` | nullOr \[str] | `null` | Restrict CI jobs to these systems. Also filters the top-level `images` output |
| `purr.hydraJobs.include` | nullOr \[str] | `null` | Outputs to mirror; `null` auto-detects |
| `purr.hydraJobs.extra` | attrs | `{}` | Extra jobs merged last, can override anything |

## Renaming the output

By default the jobs are exposed as `outputs.hydraJobs`, which Hydra looks for. `nix
flake check` treats a `hydraJobs` output specially: it evaluates it with
import-from-derivation disabled, so a host config that uses IFD can fail the check
even when `allow-import-from-derivation` is enabled in `nix.conf`.

Set `hydraJobs.as = "builds"` to expose the jobs under a different output name that
`nix flake check` does not force. A second flake can re-export them as `hydraJobs`:

```nix
# flake.nix
inputs.purr.lib.mkFlake {
  inherit inputs;
  src = ./.;
  hydraJobs = {
    enable = true;
    as = "builds";
    systems = [ "x86_64-linux" ];
  };
}
```

```nix
# hydra/flake.nix, the flake Hydra evaluates with ?dir=hydra
{
  inputs.nix-config.url = "github:you/nix-config";
  outputs = { self, nix-config }: {
    hydraJobs = nix-config.builds;
  };
}
```

The `builds` output is lazy, so `nix flake check` on the main flake never evaluates
it. Point the Hydra jobset at `github:you/nix-config?dir=hydra`.

## What gets mirrored

When `hydraJobs.include = null` (the default), purr auto-detects the available
outputs:

| Group | Source | Job |
|-------|--------|-----|
| `checks.<system>.<name>` | `checks/` | `checks.<system>.<name>` |
| `packages.<system>.<name>` | `packages/` | `packages.<system>.<name>` |
| `devShells.<system>.<name>` | `shells/` | `devShells.<system>.<name>` |
| `legacyPackages.<system>.<name>` | `legacyPackages/` | `legacyPackages.<system>.<name>` |
| `formatter.<system>` | `formatters/` | `formatter.<system>` |
| `nixosConfigurations.<system>.<host>` | `systems/` | `config.system.build.toplevel` |
| `darwinConfigurations.<system>.<host>` | `systems/` | `system` |
| `homeConfigurations.<system>.<user@host>` | `homes/` | `activationPackage` |
| `images.<host>.<format>` | host [meta](/meta) `images` | `config.system.build.images.<format>` |

`apps` are not auto-mirrored because they are `{ type = "app"; program = ...; }`
metadata rather than derivations.

Linux hosts with `images` and no `deployable = true` are excluded from
`nixosConfigurations` and the hydraJobs config groups. Their images still appear under
`images.<host>.<format>`. See
[Image-only hosts](/systems-homes#image-only-hosts).

In flake-parts mode, the per-system rows (`checks`, `packages`, `devShells`,
`legacyPackages`, `formatter`) are not mirrored. flake-parts mode mirrors
configuration outputs, images, directory jobs, and `extra`. Add anything else through
`purr.hydraJobs.extra`.

### Manual control

Set `include` to mirror only selected outputs, or to `[]` to disable mirroring:

```nix
hydraJobs.include = [ "checks" "packages" ];          # only these two
hydraJobs.include = [ ];                              # no mirroring
hydraJobs.include = [ "checks" "nixosConfigurations" "homeConfigurations" ];
```

Valid per-system names are `checks`, `packages`, `devShells`, `apps`,
`legacyPackages`, and `formatter`. Valid config names are `nixosConfigurations`,
`darwinConfigurations`, and `homeConfigurations`.

### Architecture filter

Restrict CI jobs to specific systems:

```nix
hydraJobs.systems = [ "x86_64-linux" ];
```

## Directory jobs

Custom jobs go under `hydraJobs/<group>/<job>/default.nix`. Each job is a function
that receives `{ pkgs, system, lib, inputs, namespace, ... }` and returns a
derivation, an attrset of derivations, or `null` to skip the job for that system:

```
hydraJobs/
├── build/
│   └── hello/default.nix      → hydraJobs.build.<system>.hello
└── test/
    └── unit/default.nix       → hydraJobs.test.<system>.unit
```

```nix
# hydraJobs/build/hello/default.nix
{ pkgs, system, ... }: pkgs.hello

# hydraJobs/test/unit/default.nix
{ pkgs, system, ... }:
if system == "x86_64-linux" then
  pkgs.runCommand "unit-test" { } "echo pass > $out"
else
  null   # skip this job on other systems
```

### Extra jobs

Add jobs at the top level with `extra`. This has the highest priority and can
override anything:

```nix
hydraJobs.extra = {
  ci.gitStatus = {
    "x86_64-linux".check = pkgs.runCommand "git-check" { } "true";
  };
};
```

## Example output

With `hydraJobs.enable = true`, a mkFlake project with packages, a NixOS host, and
home configs produces:

```
hydraJobs
├── build.x86_64-linux.hello         # directory job
├── checks.x86_64-linux.good         # mirrored from checks/
├── packages.x86_64-linux.hello      # mirrored from packages/
├── homeConfigurations.x86_64-linux."alice@server"   # activationPackage
├── images.server.iso                # meta images
├── nixosConfigurations.x86_64-linux.server # toplevel
└── test.x86_64-linux.unit           # directory job
```

## The `images` output

`images` is a host meta key for Linux hosts. Declare the formats in
[host meta](/meta) and purr exposes them as `images.<host>.<format>`, whether or not
hydraJobs is enabled:

```nix
# systems/x86_64-linux/server/meta.nix
{
  images = [ "iso" "qemu" ];
}
```

```bash
nix build .#images.server.iso
```

A Linux host with `images` is image-only by default and is excluded from
`nixosConfigurations` and the hydraJobs config groups. Set `deployable = true` to
expose it as a configuration as well. See
[Image-only hosts](/systems-homes#image-only-hosts).

The same declarations feed `hydraJobs.images.<host>.<format>` when hydraJobs is
enabled. See [Systems & Homes](/systems-homes) for the available formats.

# API Reference

The library exports 43 functions from a single `rec` attrset under
`inputs.purr.lib`.

## Flake builder

### `mkFlake`

Build a flake from a project directory. See the [mkFlake Usage](/mkflake) page for the
parameter table.

**Signature:** `mkFlake :: { inputs, src, ... } -> attrs`

## Attribute utilities

### `optionalAttrs`

`optionalAttrs :: cond: attrs: if cond then attrs else {}`

```nix
optionalAttrs true { foo = "bar"; }  # => { foo = "bar"; }
optionalAttrs false { foo = "bar"; } # => { }
```

## System utilities

### `defaultSystems`

`defaultSystems :: [string]`

```nix
defaultSystems  # => ["x86_64-linux" "aarch64-linux" "aarch64-darwin"]
```

### `eachSystem`

`eachSystem :: [string] -> (string -> attrs) -> attrs`

Apply a function to each system and return a system-keyed attrset.

### `eachDefaultSystem`

`eachDefaultSystem :: (string -> attrs) -> attrs`

Same as `eachSystem defaultSystems`.

## Filesystem

### `getDefaultNixFiles`

Recursively find directories containing a `default.nix`. Returns a list of
`{ path, relPath }` records, where `path` is the file and `relPath` is its directory.

## Module discovery

### `findModules`

Build a nested module tree from the `default.nix` files under
`<parentDir>/<type>`. Each directory with a `default.nix` gets a `_module` entry.

**Signature:** `findModules :: parentDir -> type -> attrs`

### `findModulesFlat`

Discover only the immediate subdirectories of `<parentDir>/<type>` that contain a
`default.nix`.

**Signature:** `findModulesFlat :: parentDir -> type -> attrs`

### `findModulesLib`

Discover lib-like modules: every `default.nix` under `<parentDir>/<type>` becomes a
nested attrset entry. The root `default.nix` is handled by
`buildImportedPurrLib`, not by this function.

**Signature:** `findModulesLib :: parentDir -> type -> attrs`

### `findModulesByName`

Discover packages using the `by-name/` layout
(`<dir>/by-name/<shard>/<name>/package.nix`). Returns a flat attrset of
`{ name = path; }`.

### `validateByName`

Validate a by-name packages directory. Returns a list of errors; an empty list means
all entries are valid. Each package's shard prefix must match its name, and each
package must have a `package.nix`.

```nix
validateByName src "packages"
# => [ ]
# or errors such as:
# => [ { name = "badshard"; shard = "xx"; error = "shard mismatch: ..."; } ]
```

### `loadModules`

Recursively load all `.nix` files from a directory.

### `readDirModules`

Read a directory into a module tree, using `_module` for a `default.nix` and
recursing into subdirectories.

### `mergeModuleTree`

Merge two module trees. When both sides define `_module`, their imports are combined.

### `discoverModules`

Multi-type module discovery. Takes a modules directory and the `moduleTypes` mapping
and returns `{ nixos, darwin, home }`.

**Signature:** `discoverModules :: modulesPath -> moduleTypes -> attrs`

### `collectModules`

Flatten a nested module attrset into a flat list for `imports`.

### `discoverSystems`

Discover system configs using the `<arch>-<format>/<name>/default.nix` layout.

### `discoverHomes`

Discover home configs using the `<arch>-<format>/<user>@<host>/default.nix` layout.

## Namespace wrapping

### `deepMapAttrs`

Map over nested attrsets, treating modules as leaves instead of recursing into them.

### `wrapModule`

Wrap one module with namespace and lib injection.

### `wrapModuleSet`

Wrap a module tree (a nested attrset of modules) with namespace and lib injection.

## Configuration builders

### `buildHomeConfigs`

Build home-manager configurations from discovered homes.

**Signature:** `buildHomeConfigs :: { discoveredHomes, discoveredSystems, inputs, ... } -> attrs`

### `buildSystemConfigs`

Build NixOS and darwin configurations from discovered systems. Linux hosts whose
[meta](/meta) declares `images` are image-only by default and are excluded from the
returned `nixosConfigurations` and `darwinConfigurations`. Set `deployable = true` in
the host meta to keep them deployable.

The result also contains:

* `configSystems`: host to system-string mapping, used by hydraJobs grouping
* `imageRecipes`: `{ host = { system; images; cfg; }; }`, consumed by
  `imagesFromConfigs`

Accepts `hostsMeta` (`{ <name> = metaAttrs; }`) merged over each host's `meta.nix`.

### `buildSystemRegistry`

Build the host metadata registry. Returns `{ hostMeta, registry }`, where `registry`
is a `name -> merged meta` map for every discovered host. The registry never touches
config values and is exposed to modules as `purr.systemMetas`. It is used by both
`buildSystemConfigs` and `buildHomeConfigs`.

### `formatOutputKey`

Map a format string to its flake output key:
`"linux" -> "nixosConfigurations"`, `"darwin" -> "darwinConfigurations"`. Throws for
other formats.

### `parseArchFormat`

`parseArchFormat :: "x86_64-linux" -> { arch = "x86_64"; format = "linux"; }`

Returns `{ arch = null; format = null; }` when the string does not match.

### `parseUserHost`

`parseUserHost :: "alice@server" -> { user = "alice"; host = "server"; }`

Returns `{ user = null; host = null; }` when the string does not match.

### `findMatchingHomes`

Find homes matching a host across all architectures. Returns a list of
`{ user, path }`.

### `imagesFromConfigs`

`imagesFromConfigs :: imageRecipes -> systemsOrNull -> { host = { format = derivation; }; }`

Extract image derivations from image recipes. For each recipe, it resolves
`cfg.config.system.build.images.<format>` lazily for the formats listed in
`recipe.images`. When `systems` is non-null, recipes are filtered by system. Used by
both the top-level `images` output and `hydraJobs.images`.

## Directory resolution

### `resolveDir`

`resolveDir :: src -> dirOption -> [candidates] -> pathOrNull`

Use the explicit option value when it is not `null`; otherwise return the first
candidate that exists under `src`.

### `resolveDirs`

`resolveDirs :: src -> dirOptions -> resolvedDirs`

Resolve every standard purr directory at once. Used by both `mkFlake` and the
flake-parts module. The result includes `hydraJobsDir`.

## Library construction

### `buildImportedPurrLib`

Build the project's custom lib. Imports the `lib/` directory and provides `inputs`,
`lib`, and `namespace` to each function module.

### `mergePurrLib`

`mergePurrLib :: nixpkgsLib -> importedLib -> namespace -> mergedLib`

Merge the project lib into nixpkgs lib under the namespace:

```nix
mergedLib = lib                    # base: nixpkgs lib
  // { ${namespace} = ownLib }     # project namespace lib
```

When `namespace` is `null`, the project lib is merged at the top level.

### `buildMergedLib`

`buildMergedLib :: { effectiveInputs, lib, importedPurrLib, namespace } -> mergedLib`

Resolve the merged lib handed to modules. The base is
`effectiveInputs.nixpkgs.lib` when available, otherwise the caller-provided `lib`.
The namespace lib is merged on top. Home configurations re-add home-manager's
`lib.hm` extension so home-manager internals keep working.

## Auto-discovery

### `autoModules`

Per-system auto-discovery for directories such as checks, shells, packages, legacy
packages, and apps. Each module is imported with the whole `pkgs` attrset spread into
its arguments, like `callPackage`, so destructuring works directly:
`{ stdenv, fetchurl, pkgs, lib, ... }`.

### `autoPackages`

Per-system package discovery for `packages/`. It works like `autoModules`, but each
discovered package is wrapped with `purrLib.makeOverridable`, so `.override` and
`.overrideAttrs` work like a `callPackage` package. Used for the
`packages.<system>.*` output and for the overlay that registers packages in `pkgs`
(`packagesToPkgs`).

### `autoFormatter`

Per-system formatter discovery. Imports `<dir>/default.nix` with the same
`pkgs`-spread arguments as `autoModules` and returns a single derivation, or `null`
when the directory is absent. Used to produce `formatter.<system>`:

```nix
# formatters/default.nix
{ pkgs, ... }: pkgs.nixfmt-rfc-style
```

### `overlayModules`

Discover and normalize overlays from a directory. Plain `final: prev: attrs` overlays
are passed through; overlays that return another overlay are normalized.

### `templateModules`

Discover flake templates from a directory.

## Hydra CI

### `filterSystems`

`filterSystems :: attrs -> systemsOrNull -> attrs`

Filter an attrset keyed by system to the given systems. Returns the attrset unchanged
when `systems` is `null`.

### `mirrorOutputs`

`mirrorOutputs :: perSystemOutputs -> names -> systemsOrNull -> attrs`

Mirror named per-system outputs into `hydraJobs.<name>.<system>.<key>` form,
optionally filtered by system.

### `hydraJobsFromDir`

`hydraJobsFromDir :: src -> dir -> systems -> systemPkgs -> lib -> namespace -> inputs -> extraArgs -> attrs`

Scan `src/<dir>/<group>/<job>/default.nix` and produce
`hydraJobs.<group>.<system>.<job>`. Each job is a function
`{ pkgs, system, lib, inputs, namespace, ... }` that returns a derivation, a
derivation attrset, or `null` to skip the job.

### `configOutputs`

Internal: exported from `lib/hydraJobs.nix` but not re-exported from
`inputs.purr.lib`.

`configOutputs :: systemConfigs -> homeConfigs -> names -> systemsOrNull -> homeSystems -> attrs`

Mirror system and home configurations into hydraJobs:
`nixosConfigurations` (toplevel), `darwinConfigurations` (system), and
`homeConfigurations` (activationPackage), grouped by system.

### `buildHydraJobs`

`buildHydraJobs :: { src, hydraJobsDir, hydraSystems, hydraJobsInclude, hydraJobsExtra, systemPkgs, perSystemOutputs, systemConfigs, homeConfigs, homeSystems, lib, namespace, inputs, extraArgs } -> attrs`

Combine the hydraJobs sources: directory jobs, mirrored per-system outputs, config
outputs, images, and `hydraJobsExtra` (highest priority).
